text:
For one morning the Avalanche held their breath over Cale Makar. He said he felt really good, he played against Toronto, and Colorado moved on, which is the right word for a team at 11-6-2 with a 96% chance at the playoffs in our simulations and a projection of about 106 points.

The engine is familiar. Nathan MacKinnon is playing at a pace headlines are calling historic, and his line with Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas is plus 11 at five on five. Makar and Devon Toews get 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) together, and Toews is on a tear: 11 points in 10 games against 6.3 expected. Overall Colorado owns 55% of the chances, which is a contender's number.

The worry is the gap between that and the scoreboard. The Avs have scored nearly 13 more goals than their chances deserved, the biggest finishing surplus of any team we looked at this week, and some of that will come back. Josh Manson is reported out up to eight weeks, which thins a right side that already leans on Makar. And Gabriel Landeskog's shot volume, slow early, is only now creeping back, as Evan Rawal pointed out.

Mackenzie Blackwood has been through a lot to get back to this crease, and his steadiness matters more than any hot streak. What to watch: whether the second line of Nazem Kadri, Brock Nelson and Landeskog grows into a real answer when MacKinnon gets checked.
headline: Colorado is very good and a little lucky
